description:
The Notepad equivalent for Markdown

A lightweight, minimalist Markdown viewer and text editor built for productivity.
What's new in 2.8.3
A release about speed, plus a handful of fixes.
- Faster startup. Markpad starts with English only and fetches your language the first time it is needed, so the startup code is about a fifth smaller. Code highlighting, maths and diagrams load only when a document uses them. A plain-text document no longer downloads about 1.9 MB of libraries.
- Large files open faster. Opening a file used to render it twice. It renders once now. Documents with lots of maths no longer slow down sharply as they grow: a 1.6 MB test document went from 3.3 s to 0.12 s to render.
- Typing and scrolling do less work. The word count waits for a pause in typing and is skipped when it is hidden. Scrolling no longer re-reads the whole document. Folding and the outline share one pass instead of two. The preview parses each update once fewer and finds lines on scroll without walking the whole page.
- No more freezes on paste or save. Pasting a large image and saving the session no longer block every window. An external save that touches the file several times now reloads once.
- Tables wrap between words. A short column next to a long one no longer breaks words in the middle. A table that still does not fit scrolls sideways.
- Exports keep your fonts. PDF and HTML exports now carry the preview's font, font size, code font, code font size and highlight colour.
- Wayland paste works. On Linux under Wayland, paste reads the system clipboard instead of the last thing copied inside Markpad.
- Small fixes. Dragging a document over the editor says Drop to Open. The settings dialog no longer grows a little every time its header is clicked.

Note
Windows SmartScreen Notice: Windows executables are not signed with an Authenticode certificate, so SmartScreen shows them as an unrecognized app. Click "More info" → "Run anyway". The antivirus heuristic that used to flag the portable .exe no longer does.
Note
macOS folder access: Coming from 2.7.x or earlier, macOS asks for folder access once more after this update. From now on the grant carries across updates.
If you gave Markpad Full Disk Access in 2.7.x or earlier, that grant no longer applies, and macOS asks each time Markpad saves to Desktop or Documents. Renew it once: in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access, select Markpad, remove it with −, then add /Applications/Markpad.app again with +.
The two Windows files differ only in that one installs and one does not.
Package managers: choco install markpad-app (Windows), brew install --cask markpad (macOS), sudo snap install markpad (Linux).
What Markpad renders
Every syntax Markpad renders is in one document — download markdown-syntax.md (简体中文) and open it in Markpad: the preview shows each feature working, the editor beside it shows how each one is written. Give the same file to an AI and it knows exactly what Markpad can render: ask it to reformat a document you already have, or to write a new one that uses the whole range — callouts, tables, footnotes, maths, diagrams — and open the result here. Read it on GitHub.
